failure_summary.description: Answers followed a contextually salient subtype or example, or an expanded term, instead of the answer granularity called for by the clue.
The instruction to omit optional middle initials conflicts with retaining conventional, context-supported identifying initials.
The title spelling differed from the gold answer, though the retrieved sources used the agent's form.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers matching clue scope and avoiding examples when a general term is requested, so repeating those rules would not address the ignored guidance. The name-form guidance does contain a direct contradiction that plausibly caused the dropped initial; revise it to retain supported identifying elements without adding unsupported ones. The title-spacing mismatch is not patched because the agent followed the source-supported title form.

edits.target: Use the supported conventional name form: expand a nickname to the full given name when the evidence supports it, and omit optional middle initials or generational suffixes unless requested or needed to distinguish the person. Thus prefer Patricia Hearst, Lyndon Johnson, and Alan Shepard when those are the supported answer forms. Conversely, do not shorten a proper publication title by removing a word that belongs to it: when the journal is named Forbes magazine, return Forbes magazine rather than Forbes.
edits.content: Use the supported conventional name form: expand a nickname to the full given name when the evidence supports it; do not add unsupported initials or generational suffixes, but retain conventional identifying name elements, including middle initials, when they are supported by context. Do not drop a name element solely because it is technically optional. Conversely, do not shorten a proper publication title by removing a word that belongs to it: when the journal is named Forbes magazine, return Forbes magazine rather than Forbes.
